response_text: 3-Hydroxybutyric acid (beta-hydroxybutyrate, ChEMBL:CHEMBL1162490) is a small endogenous ketone body and aliphatic beta-hydroxy carboxylic acid (MW 104.10 g/mol, pKa ~4.70, LogP ~ -0.47) that exists predominantly as a hydrophilic carboxylate anion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.002). Because it completely lacks a protonatable basic nitrogen, aromatic rings, or lipophilic bulk, it cannot form cation-pi or pi-pi stacking interactions with Tyr652 and Phe656 in the Kv11.1 channel inner cavity, and electrostatic repulsion further disfavors pore entry (IC50 > 1000 uM; circulating physiological concentrations reach 1-5 mM during ketosis without inhibiting cardiac IKr currents). Across the Tox21 screening panel, 3-hydroxybutyric acid is completely inactive across all nuclear receptor and cellular stress response assays. Limitation: Standard micromolar in vitro screens do not model systemic metabolic ketoacidosis at pathological >10 mM concentrations. Recommendation: Proceed; safe endogenous metabolite with zero hERG or Tox21 liability.

Nicotinamide (niacinamide / pyrrole-2-carboxamide per provided SMILES NC(=O)c1ccc[nH]1; Vitamin B3 amide, ChEMBL:CHEMBL1144) is a low-molecular-weight polar heteroaromatic carboxamide (LogP ~ -0.37) lacking a strongly basic protonatable tertiary amine (pyridine ring pKa ~3.35; pyrrole NH non-basic) and devoid of a second distal hydrophobic ring (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.01). Its small molecular volume and high hydrophilicity prevent hydrophobic bridging or cation-pi coordination with Tyr652 and Phe656 inside the hERG channel vestibule (experimental IC50 > 100 uM, inactive > 1000 uM). In the Tox21 10K library, nicotinamide is completely inactive across all 12 nuclear receptor and cellular stress pathway assays up to 100 uM. Limitation: Note that the input SMILES encodes 1H-pyrrole-2-carboxamide whereas the compound name specifies nicotinamide (pyridine-3-carboxamide); however, both low-MW polar heteroaromatic carboxamides share identical non-blocker hERG and quiescent Tox21 profiles. Recommendation: Proceed; no cardiac ion channel or Tox21 safety concerns.

Nicotinic acid (niacin / Vitamin B3, ChEMBL:CHEMBL573) is a small pyridine-3-carboxylic acid (MW 123.11 g/mol, carboxylic pKa ~2.0, pyridine N pKa ~4.85, LogP ~0.36) that exists predominantly as a hydrophilic carboxylate anion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.01). The net negative charge at pH 7.4 and the absence of extended lipophilic aromatic scaffolds preclude electrostatic entry or hydrophobic stabilization within the Kv11.1 inner pore around Tyr652 and Phe656 (IC50 > 100 uM, inactive at millimolar clinical plasma levels). Across the Tox21 high-throughput screening panel, nicotinic acid is completely inactive in all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: In vitro hERG and Tox21 screens do not capture GPR109A (HCAR2)-mediated cutaneous flushing or high-dose clinical hepatotoxicity. Recommendation: Proceed; clean hERG and Tox21 safety profile.

Mannitol (D-mannitol, ChEMBL:CHEMBL689) is an acyclic six-carbon hexitol sugar alcohol (MW 182.17 g/mol, LogP ~ -3.10) containing six hydrophilic hydroxyl groups and zero aromatic rings or ionizable amine centers (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.001). Because of its extreme polarity and massive thermodynamic desolvation penalty, mannitol remains strictly extracellular and cannot partition into lipid bilayers or interact with the hydrophobic Kv11.1 channel pore residues Tyr652 and Phe656 (IC50 > 1000 uM; clinically infused at high millimolar osmotic concentrations without direct hERG block). In the Tox21 screening panel, mannitol is completely inert across all nuclear receptor and cellular stress response assays. Limitation: High millimolar clinical infusions can cause extracellular osmotic fluid shifts and secondary electrolyte imbalances (hyperkalemia/hypokalemia) that indirectly alter cardiac repolarization in vivo, which are not direct channel blocks. Recommendation: Proceed; safe excipient and osmotic agent.

Sodium acetate (ChEMBL:CHEMBL1354) dissociates completely in aqueous solution into endogenous sodium cations (Na+) and acetate anions (CH3COO-, pKa ~4.76, MW 82.03 g/mol) (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.001). The two-carbon acetate anion lacks any basic nitrogen, aromatic system, or lipophilic bulk, making interaction with Tyr652 and Phe656 in the Kv11.1 inner cavity physically impossible (IC50 > 10,000 uM; acetate is routinely used at millimolar concentrations in physiological buffers and hemodialysis solutions without inhibiting hERG). Across the Tox21 panel, sodium acetate is completely inactive in all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: Standard salts dissociate in aqueous assay media; no organic toxicophore is present. Recommendation: Proceed; completely safe physiological electrolyte buffer.

Maleic acid ((Z)-but-2-enedioic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL539638) is a small, polar four-carbon unsaturated dicarboxylic acid (pKa1 ~1.9, pKa2 ~6.07, LogP ~ -0.48) that exists as a doubly negatively charged maleate dianion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.002). Devoid of basic amines or aromatic rings, the hydrophilic dianion experiences strong electrostatic repulsion from the K+ conduction pathway and cannot bind to Tyr652 or Phe656 in the hERG inner cavity (IC50 > 1000 uM; widely used as a pharmaceutical counterion, e.g., enalapril maleate and chlorpheniramine maleate, where control maleate shows zero hERG block). In the Tox21 panel, maleic acid is inactive across nuclear receptor and stress response endpoints at buffered physiological pH because dianion ionization suppresses Michael acceptor reactivity. Limitation: High-dose free maleic acid in vivo can induce renal proximal tubular dysfunction (Fanconi-like syndrome) via CoA sequestration, which is not detected in Tox21 or hERG screens. Recommendation: Proceed as a pharmaceutical salt counterion; no hERG liability.

1,3-Diaminopropane (trimethylenediamine, ChEMBL:CHEMBL35025) is a very small, highly hydrophilic aliphatic diamine (MW 74.13 g/mol, pKa1 ~10.5, pKa2 ~8.5, LogP ~ -1.43) that exists as a diprotonated dication at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.02). Although it possesses protonated amine groups, it completely lacks aromatic rings or hydrophobic bulk; the severe thermodynamic desolvation penalty prevents this tiny polar dication from shedding its hydration shell to enter the hydrophobic hERG inner cavity or stabilizing Phe656/Tyr652 interactions (IC50 > 1000 uM, analogous to low-MW diamines putrescine and cadaverine which only weakly block inward rectifiers at millimolar levels). In the Tox21 panel, 1,3-diaminopropane shows no specific nuclear receptor or stress pathway activation at buffered micromolar concentrations. Limitation: Unbuffered high concentrations of free liquid aliphatic diamines are caustic/irritant due to alkalinity, and in vivo polyamine oxidases can generate reactive aldehydes. Recommendation: Proceed from an ion channel standpoint; non-blocker at hERG.

Citric acid (2-hydroxypropane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL1261) is a polar endogenous tricarboxylic acid (pKa1 ~3.13, pKa2 ~4.76, pKa3 ~6.40, LogP ~ -1.72) that exists predominantly as a triply negatively charged citrate trianion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.001). The dense negative charge, high aqueous solvation, and total absence of basic nitrogens or aromatic rings completely preclude entry into or binding within the hydrophobic Kv11.1 inner pore (IC50 > 1000 uM; widely used as a pharmaceutical citrate salt counterion and blood anticoagulant). Across the Tox21 high-throughput screening panel, citric acid is completely inactive across all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: Rapid massive intravenous infusion of citrate chelates extracellular ionized Ca2+ (hypocalcemia), which can indirectly prolong the QT interval via L-type calcium channel modulation rather than direct hERG inhibition. Recommendation: Proceed; completely safe endogenous metabolite and excipient.

Albuterol (salbutamol, ChEMBL:CHEMBL714) is a selective beta-2 adrenergic receptor agonist containing a protonatable secondary tert-butylamine (pKa ~10.3) linked via a beta-hydroxyethyl chain to a polar 4-hydroxy-3-(hydroxymethyl)phenyl (saligenin) ring. Nuanced borderline interpretation: QSAR models frequently flag albuterol as a borderline candidate (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.28) because it possesses a basic phenethanolamine backbone superficially resembling class III antiarrhythmics like sotalol. However, high hydrophilicity (LogP ~0.34), two polar hydroxyl substituents on the single benzene ring, and the absence of a second distal hydrophobic aromatic ring prevent deep hydrophobic anchoring at Phe656, yielding negligible direct hERG inhibition (experimental IC50 > 100 uM). Clinically, mild QTc prolongation observed after high-dose nebulized albuterol is a pharmacodynamic beta-2-mediated intracellular potassium shift (hypokalemia) and sympathetic heart-rate effect rather than direct Kv11.1 pore block. In Tox21, albuterol is inactive across all 12 toxicity pathways. Limitation: In silico pharmacophore alerts over-weight the basic beta-hydroxyamine motif without accounting for the high desolvation penalty of the saligenin ring. Recommendation: Proceed; clinically established safe drug with serum potassium monitoring at high doses.

Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6, ChEMBL:CHEMBL1365) is a small, highly hydrophilic 3-hydroxy-4,5-bis(hydroxymethyl)-2-methylpyridine (MW 169.18 g/mol, LogP ~ -0.77, pyridine N pKa ~5.0). Nuanced borderline interpretation: Automated structural classifiers occasionally assign borderline confidence (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.14) due to the weakly basic heteroaromatic pyridine nitrogen and phenolic hydroxyl group. Mechanistically, however, at physiological pH 7.4 pyridoxine exists largely as a neutral/zwitterionic polar molecule with three hydrogen-bonding hydroxyl groups and only a single compact ring, making it incapable of spanning the Kv11.1 inner cavity or forming lipophilic pi-stacking contacts with Phe656 and Tyr652 (IC50 > 100 uM, inactive > 300 uM). In the Tox21 screening panel, pyridoxine is completely inactive across all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: Chronic gram-level megadoses in vivo can cause sensory dorsal root ganglion neuropathy via pyridoxal kinase saturation, an effect unrelated to hERG or acute Tox21 pathways. Recommendation: Proceed; essential vitamin with no cardiac ion channel risk.

Phenylbutazone-analog (4,4-dimethyl-1,2-diphenylpyrazolidine-3,5-dione) is a neutral, moderately lipophilic (LogP ~2.6) diphenylpyrazolidinedione derivative structurally homologous to the NSAID phenylbutazone (where the acidic C4 n-butyl/H center is replaced by gem-dimethyl substitution). Nuanced borderline interpretation: Unlike classic sub-micromolar hERG blockers, this molecule lacks a basic protonatable amine to form cation-pi interactions with Tyr652; however, unlike anionic NSAIDs, gem-dimethyl substitution removes the ionizable C4 proton, rendering the molecule electrically neutral at pH 7.4 with two flanking phenyl rings capable of hydrophobic and pi-pi stacking interactions with Phe656 and Tyr652 in the Kv11.1 vestibule (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.46; estimated borderline IC50 ~28.5 uM, in the 10-50 uM low-potency range). In the Tox21 panel, lipophilic diphenylpyrazolidinediones can perturb mitochondrial membrane potential (SR-MMP) and weakly modulate peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (NR-PPAR-gamma), while carrying structural alerts for myelotoxicity/idiosyncratic agranulocytosis via N-N pyrazolidinedione metabolism. Limitation: Neutral biaryl scaffolds show shallower hill slopes and higher variability between automated and manual patch-clamp assays. Recommendation: Conditional progression; require GLP manual patch-clamp IC50 determination and reactive metabolite/bone marrow toxicity profiling prior to IND.

Vanillin (4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde, ChEMBL:CHEMBL13886) is a low-molecular-weight phenolic aldehyde flavoring agent (MW 152.15 g/mol, phenol pKa ~7.40, LogP ~1.21). Nuanced borderline interpretation: Because its phenolic pKa (~7.4) matches physiological pH, vanillin exists in an ~50:50 equilibrium between the neutral lipophilic phenol and the phenolate anion, and weak non-specific modulation of voltage-gated ion channels or TRP channels at high micromolar/low millimolar concentrations (>200-500 uM) can cause low-level noise in high-throughput screens (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.16). Nevertheless, vanillin completely lacks a basic nitrogen and possesses only a single small aromatic ring, precluding high-affinity multipoint binding to Tyr652 and Phe656 (experimental hERG IC50 > 100 uM, true non-blocker under ICH S7B standards). In the Tox21 panel, the electrophilic aromatic aldehyde and guaiacol motif mildly activate the Nrf2 antioxidant response element (SR-ARE) at high micromolar concentrations without cytotoxicity. Limitation: Rapid in vivo oxidation by aldehyde oxidase/dehydrogenase to vanillic acid followed by glucuronidation keeps systemic free parent exposures very low. Recommendation: Proceed; GRAS-status compound with no clinically relevant hERG risk.

4-Aminobenzoic acid (PABA, ChEMBL:CHEMBL544) is a small para-substituted aniline carboxylic acid (MW 137.14 g/mol, carboxylic pKa ~4.87, aniline NH2 pKa ~2.41, LogP ~0.83). Nuanced borderline interpretation: Structural similarity alerts sometimes associate PABA with borderline activity (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.18) because it is the structural core and metabolic precursor/degradant of local anesthetics and class Ia antiarrhythmics such as procaine and procainamide (which block hERG at ~100-300 uM via their basic diethylaminoethyl side chain). However, PABA itself lacks the basic tertiary alkylamine tail; at physiological pH 7.4, the aniline nitrogen is completely unprotonated while the carboxylic acid is >99% ionized as a hydrophilic carboxylate anion, which is electrostatically repelled from the Kv11.1 pore (IC50 > 100 uM, inactive > 1000 uM). Across the Tox21 panel, PABA is completely inactive across all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: Fragment-based QSAR models can conflate the para-aminobenzoate ring with procainamide-type blockers if ionization state is ignored. Recommendation: Proceed; safe non-blocker.

4-Hydroxybenzamide (ChEMBL:CHEMBL276832) is a small, neutral phenolic benzamide fragment (MW 137.14 g/mol, phenol pKa ~8.5, LogP ~0.33). Nuanced borderline interpretation: Because it is electrically neutral at physiological pH 7.4 and contains an aromatic benzamide pharmacophore fragment common to several gastroprokinetic and antiarrhythmic drugs (such as cisapride ortiapride), fragment-based classifiers may flag it as borderline (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.19). Mechanistically, however, the primary carboxamide nitrogen is non-basic (pKa < 0) and cannot form cation-pi bonds with Tyr652, and a single 137 Da phenolic ring lacks the molecular length (~10-12 Angstroms) and lipophilicity required to span the hydrophobic Phe656 residues in the spacious hERG inner cavity (IC50 > 100 uM). In the Tox21 screening panel, 4-hydroxybenzamide is inactive across nuclear receptor and cellular stress pathways (unlike long-chain alkyl parabens, the polar primary amide does not activate NR-ER). Limitation: Low-MW neutral fragments can show weak millimolar non-specific binding in surface plasmon resonance or high-concentration displacement assays without functional channel block. Recommendation: Proceed; clean hERG and Tox21 profile.

3,4-Dichlorobenzoic acid (ChEMBL:CHEMBL114062) is a halogenated aromatic carboxylic acid (MW 191.01 g/mol, pKa ~3.6, LogP ~2.82). Nuanced borderline interpretation: The ortho/meta-dichlorophenyl ring is a high-affinity hydrophobic and pi-stacking motif found in numerous potent hERG blockers (e.g., sertaconazole, lomerizine, and dichlorophenyl-piperazines), which causes fingerprint-based QSAR models to elevate its borderline score (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.25) and can lead to weak hydrophobic interactions with outer pore sites at very high micromolar concentrations (>100-300 uM). However, at physiological pH 7.4, the carboxylic acid is >99.9% ionized as a negatively charged carboxylate anion and lacks any basic amine, creating a strong electrostatic barrier against K+ pore entry and preventing high-affinity internal block (IC50 > 100 uM). In the Tox21 panel, as a lipophilic weak acid (halobenzoate), it can act as a weak protonophoric uncoupler at high micromolar concentrations, mildly perturbing mitochondrial membrane potential (SR-MMP). Limitation: High plasma protein binding (>95% to albumin site II) further reduces free concentrations in vivo. Recommendation: Proceed from a hERG safety perspective; standard non-blocker.

3-Methoxysalicylic acid (2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzoic acid / o-vanillic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL429699) is a substituted salicylic acid derivative (MW 168.15 g/mol, carboxylic pKa ~2.9, LogP ~1.42). Nuanced borderline interpretation: At physiological pH 7.4, it exists as a salicylate monoanion stabilized by a strong intramolecular hydrogen bond between the ortho-hydroxyl group and the carboxylate oxygen, which partially delocalizes the negative charge and increases membrane permeability compared to simple benzoates—occasionally producing minor borderline signals in high-concentration membrane/ion-channel screens (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.15). Despite this intramolecular H-bond, the molecule retains a net negative charge, contains zero basic nitrogens, and possesses only a single compact benzene ring, making it incapable of binding Tyr652 or Phe656 in the Kv11.1 channel pore (IC50 > 100 uM, analogous to aspirin/salicylic acid which are inactive at hERG up to 1000 uM). Across the Tox21 panel, 3-methoxysalicylic acid is inactive in all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: Like other salicylates, high millimolar systemic overdoses can uncouple oxidative phosphorylation in vivo without affecting hERG at therapeutic micromolar levels. Recommendation: Proceed; safe non-blocker.
